bugLogs.title: Product prices on search results have insufficient color contrast
affected_users: older users with declining contrast sensitivity
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the search results page
Observe the price text in the 3rd, 4th, and 5th result items
Note the light gray color (#bdbdbd) of the price text against the white background
Measure the contrast ratio using a color contrast tool
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Price text should have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background color, per WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criterion 1.4.3
bugLogs.actual_behavior: Price text has a contrast ratio of only 1.87:1 (foreground #bdbdbd on background #ffffff), which fails the 4.5:1 minimum requirement
bugLogs.suggested_fix: In the CSS rule for .result:nth-child(3) > div > span, change color from #bdbdbd to #757575 (4.61:1 on #ffffff; measured 1.87:1, required 4.5:1).
bugLogs.element_selector: .result:nth-child(3) > div > span, .result:nth-child(4) > div > span, .result:nth-child(5) > div > span

bugLogs.title: Product images missing alt text on search results page
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the search results page
Locate the product images for trail, road, and light shoes
Use a screen reader to inspect the images
Observe that no alternative text is announced for any of the three images
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each product image should have a descriptive alt attribute that conveys the product name and key visual characteristics, allowing screen reader users to understand the product being displayed.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The three product images (shoe-trail.jpg, shoe-road.jpg, shoe-light.jpg) have no alt attribute, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, and no role='none' or role='presentation', so screen readers announce them as generic 'image' with no context.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add descriptive alt attributes to each image: alt='Trail running shoe, side view' to img[src$='shoe-trail.jpg'], alt='Road running shoe, side view' to img[src$='shoe-road.jpg'], and alt='Lightweight running shoe, side view' to img[src$='shoe-light.jpg']. Ensure alt text describes the product type and key visual features.

bugLogs.title: Next page link lacks accessible name
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the search results page
Locate the pagination control for the next page
Focus the 'next' link using a screen reader or keyboard
Listen to the announced name of the link
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The link should have a discernible accessible name that describes its purpose, such as 'Next page' or 'Go to page 2', so assistive technologies can announce it correctly.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The link is empty and has no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title attribute, resulting in no accessible name being announced.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add aria-label='Next page' to the anchor element with selector 'a.next' or add visible text content inside the link.

bugLogs.title: Sort dropdown missing accessible name
steps_to_reproduce: Navigate to the search results page
Focus the sort dropdown element with id 'sort'
Listen to the screen reader announcement for the element
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The select element should have a programmatically determinable accessible name, such as 'Sort by', so assistive technologies can announce its purpose.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The select element has no associated label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby, so screen readers announce it as a generic 'combobox' without context.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add a visible label associated with the select element: <label for="sort">Sort by</label> before the <select id="sort"> element, or add aria-label="Sort by" to the select element.
